objectives.text: greet a classmate and ask and answer “What's your name?” “My name's Mila.”
name things in the classroom: a board, a clock, a desk and a globe
point to classroom things and ask and answer “What's this?” “It's a map.”
read My Classroom, about a school in Bangladesh, and compare it with their classroom
hear the difference between the a and e sounds and read short words with each
introduce two friends to each other with “Mila, this is Matt.”
name school things: a bag, a crayon, an eraser and a pencil
ask “Is this a bag?” and answer “Yes, it is.” or “No, it isn't.”
read In My School Bag, from Mexico, and say what they carry in their own bag
hear, say and read short words with the e and i sounds

units.title: School Link 1 · Schools around the world

objectives.text: learn how schools around the world are alike and different
tell one thing about a school in another country
draw and label a poster of their dream school
present their dream school poster to the class in a few sentences
ask “How are you?” and answer “I'm fine.” or “I'm great. Thank you.”
name farm animals: a chicken, a cow, a goat, a goose, a horse and a sheep
use “What's this?” for near things and “What's that?” for things far away
read Favorite Farm Animals, from Australia, and say which farm animal they like best
sort words by their middle sound, o or u, and read them aloud
introduce a friend to an adult and say “Nice to meet you.”
name things in a park: a bench, a duck, a pond and a picnic table
ask “Is that a pond?” and answer “Yes, it is.” or “No, it isn't.”
read Different Parks and tell how the parks are alike and different
tell b and p apart at the start of words, like bench and pond
learn what sounds different animals make and match each sound to an animal
say in English what sound an animal makes, like “A cow says moo.”
make an animal puppet and give it a name and a sound
use their puppet to act out a short animal talk with a partner
ask a friend “What's your favorite color?” and ask back “What about you?”
name eleven colors, including pink, gray, orange and purple
ask and answer “What color is this?” and “Is this green?” about things around them
read National Flags and name the colors on the flags of Malaysia, Sudan, France and Jamaica
hear whether a word ends in b or p and read words with each
ask “What's your favorite fruit?” and answer “I like bananas.” or “I like bananas too.”
name fruits for more than one: apples, grapes, peaches and watermelons
ask “What are these?” and answer “They're apples.” about more than one thing
read Favorite Fruits, from India, and tell their own favorite fruit
tell d and t apart at the start of words they hear and read
learn that fruits have seeds inside and that seeds can grow into new plants
describe the seeds of a fruit by their color, size and number
make a poster of their favorite fruit, showing its color and its seeds
tell the class about their fruit poster in two or three sentences
say “Happy birthday!” and ask and answer “How old are you?” “I'm seven.”
count from one to ten and name a circle, a diamond, a rectangle and a triangle
ask and answer “How many circles?” “Seven circles.” by counting shapes in a picture
read A World of Numbers and tell where we see numbers every day
hear whether a word ends in d or t and read words with each
say “Oops! I'm sorry.” and answer “That's OK.” after a small accident
name school supplies at a store: glue sticks, markers, rulers and scissors
ask “Are these rulers?” and answer “Yes, they are.” or “No, they aren't.”
read Tim's School Things, from the UK, and compare Tim's things with their own
tell the c sound and the g sound apart in words they hear and read
listen to a short story problem and add or take away to find the answer
say a number sentence out loud, like “Three plus two is five.”
make a shape book with circles, squares, triangles and other shapes
read their shape book to a partner, naming and counting each shape
give a present with “This is for you.” and ask and answer “What is it?”
name family members: grandma, grandpa, mom, dad, brother and sister
use he and she to ask and answer “Who is he?” “He's Mila's brother.”
read Families, Big and Small, about families in Italy, Japan and Zambia, and compare them with their own
tell f and v sounds apart in words they hear and read
greet an adult with “Good morning, Dr. Brown.” and say “I don't feel good.”
name jobs: a cook, a doctor, a nurse and a police officer
ask “Is she a teacher?” and answer “Yes, she is.” or “No, she isn't.”
read Jobs and Places and match each job to the place where people do it
tell f and p sounds apart in words they hear and read
learn how different animals live together in families
tell about one animal family: who is in it and where it lives
make a mobile of an animal family with a label for each animal
show their mobile and say who each animal is, like “This is the baby.”
suggest a game with “Let's play!” and say “I'm thirsty.” “Me too.”
name and act out feelings: happy, sad, angry, tired, hungry and thirsty
look at a picture and ask “Are they happy?” and answer “Yes, they are.” or “No, they aren't.”
read Feelings and say how the people in the pictures feel
hear and say l and r clearly and read words that start with each
say goodbye with “Goodbye.” and “See you later.” and say “I'm tired now.”
name pets: birds, cats, rabbits and turtles
ask “Do you like dogs?” and answer “Yes, I do.” or “No, I don't.”
read My Pets, about pets in China, Egypt, Belgium and Colombia, and tell about a pet
tell m and n sounds apart in words they hear and read
read a simple bar graph and tell which bar is the tallest
ask friends “Do you like cats?” to find out which pets they like
make a bar graph of the different pets their friends like
tell what their bar graph shows, like “Five friends like cats.”
